description: List a website's open audit issues (like a bug tracker: each issue is one failing rule with occurrences across pages, numbered per website). Returns issues sorted by severity. `total`, `returned` and `has_more` describe the issues matching YOUR filters; `website_totals` (by_status, active_by_severity: open and in_progress) always counts the whole website regardless of filters, so the two can differ (it replaces the earlier `severity_summary` and `status_counts` fields). Rows omit the long `recommendation` (use get_rule with the row's rule_id, or get_issue, or pass include_recommendation: true). Use the issue number with get_issue for full detail and comments. Filter by status/severity/category to narrow down. After a smart audit each row also carries `provenance`: "fresh" means this audit re-checked the issue, "carried" means it only survives because its pages were not re-crawled this audit, so `last_seen_at` (when it was last actually observed) is the evidence date, not `last_detected_at`, and a carried issue needs a re-crawl to confirm before you act on it; "unrendered" means its page has never been rendered in any scan (no earlier observation, no `last_seen_at`). Both keys are absent when the website's audits carry none. This is a per-website tracker spanning audits, not a per-run count: one rule failing on 600 pages is ONE issue here, and an issue stays open until an audit re-checks it. So the open count is expected to be far smaller than a run's issues_found (list_audits) or a report's failed+warnings, and the two are not comparable (#1700). To compare runs, use health_score from list_audits. `coverage` (snake_case keys) is present ONLY when the website's latest audit did not cover every page it knows of (sampled by its level or page limit, stopped on time, or a queue left over): `audited_pages` of `known_pages` (`not_audited_pages` is the gap, a floor), split into `carried_pages` (known from earlier audits and not re-checked now: their earlier findings ARE in this list, carried, and stay open until a later audit re-checks them) and `unaudited_pages` (found but never audited: a problem there would NOT appear in this list), plus `capped`, `time_stopped`, `max_pages` and `page_types` (the sampled types as `{type, discovered, audited}`). The list can then be shorter than the site's real problems when `unaudited_pages` is above 0: say so, and offer a deeper audit (run_audit with level full). It does not mean any listed issue is in doubt. Absent means every known page was audited.

category.description: Filter by rule category code (e.g. seo, performance, security).

include_recommendation.description: Include each issue's full recommendation text (default false; see get_rule).

status.description: Filter by issue status (omit for all statuses).

website_id.description: Website id from list_websites, run_audit, or list_audits.

name: list_issues
title: List website issues
